newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher in quiet session.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to see some follow through on Friday's rally and open higher, but analysts say that trading will be quiet with the bond market closed for the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.
"It's a semi-holiday today so trading will be light," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"Bonds, banks and the government are all shut down so all you can do is look at the individual earnings reports to see what kind of influence they will have on the stock market."

Much higher than forecast third quarter earnings from Chrysler Corp will give the market further impetus to the upside, said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. Chrysler reported quarterly earnings per share of $0.93, compared to $0.45 in 1995 and well above the First Call estimate of $0.71.

"With the absence of economic data and record earnings from Chrysler, we'll probably see a better day for stocks, one that takes us a step closer to a 6000 close on the Dow," Cardillo said. "Historically, Columbus Day has generally seen the market moving up."
Cardillo said that he expected the Dow industrials to open five points higher and that the day could see the market up by about 15 at the close.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see the Dow up 20 intraday although I don't think we have enough strength for the market to close above 6000 today," he said.

Also reporting third quarter earnings Monday is bellwether Intel Corp. According to First Call, the company is expected after the close of trading to report earnings per share of $1.25 a share compared to $1.02 in the year-ago period.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was up 61 points at 21,029.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up six at 4034.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, Intel was down 1/2 at 104-7/8. Ford Motor Co was up 1/4 at 32.
Shares in General Motors Corp were off 3/8 at 49-3/4. Shares in Archer Daniels Midland Co rose 1/4 to 20-7/8, a new high.
The dollar was directionless in Tokyo and hovered just above 1.53 marks in Europe.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column writes that Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp is too big, with revenue of nearly $19 billion in the past 12 months, to maintain its pace of growth.

The New York Times Market Place writes Dow Jones & Co Inc earnings are falling as its electronic price and news service Telerate struggles against the competition after failing to invest in technology.
